subject: Hudson Retail - sudden throughput regression & exec bridge
content:
From: Emily Chen <e.chen@hudsonretail.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — checkout timeouts 15:00 PDT

Jonas —

We started seeing a large spike in checkout latency across our US region at ~15:00 PDT. Error rate climbed to ~5.4% and p95 latency jumped >1.2s; throughput dropped ~40% on peak traffic. Impacting both guest and logged-in flows. Our ops flagged numerous tokenization/serve errors in logs (attached snapshot). Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We are holding a customer-facing banner soon.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
VP Product, Hudson Retail

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:28:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — checkout timeouts 15:00 PDT

Emily — thanks for the flag and the logs. Laura and Marissa are on standby. Initial telemetry shows a sudden increase in KV-cache misses and downstream RPC retries on the model pool serving Hudson's dedicated allocation. Error traces reference token-length spikes in requests (longer user messages after a marketing push). I'm opening an exec bridge now — will provide cadence and customer-facing language.

Immediate next steps (I):
- Laura: validate model variant routing and check for recent config/roll changes.
- Marissa: check dedicated pool capacity and autoscale triggers.
- Sean (on-call SRE): capture live p95/p99 panels and snapshot current req histogram.

Emily — expect our first customer update within 30min.

— Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:34:45 -0700
Subject: RE: Production latency spike — checkout timeouts 15:00 PDT

Bridge notes (15:34):
- Observed: sudden skew in request length distribution starting 14:58 PDT. Median token length up ~3x for Hudson-specific traffic; KV-cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 21% on the dedicated pool.
- Likely root cause: a payload-pattern change (longer system prompts/metadata) driving cache thrash plus model kernel contention under existing bin-packing. No code deploy on Redwood side at that time.
- Short-term mitigations applied:
  * Forced routing to fallback quantized variant (lower memory pressure) for 20% of traffic to reduce pausing;
  * Increased dedicated pool node count by +30% (manual scale) to restore capacity;
  * Enabled short-lived request-throttling at ingress for noisy keys to protect critical checkout paths.
- Observed impact (15:32): error rate down from 5.4% -> 2.1%, throughput recovering to ~85% of baseline, p95 trending down but not yet stable.

Action items (owner/due):
- Marissa: continue scale stabilization, watch autoscale oscillation (15m cadence).
- Sean: collect KV-cache heatmaps and attach to the Jira.
- Grace: draft exec one-pager for Hudson execs + suggested customer comm (see attached draft).
- Jonas: coordinate any SLA credit ask and keep product/customer execs notified.

Laura Bennett
Director, Serving Reliability

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Emily Chen <e.chen@hudsonretail.com>, David Park <david.park@hudsonretail.com>, Hudson SRE <sre@hudsonretail.com>

Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:55:02 -0700
Subject: Hudson status update — mitigation in progress

Emily / David —
Quick update from the Redwood side: we identified a sudden increase in token lengths from a subset of requests that caused KV-cache thrash on your dedicated pool. We executed the following mitigations and will continue to monitor:
- Increased pool capacity (+30% nodes) to regain throughput;
- Partial routing to a lower-memory quantized model to reduce kernel contention;
- Short-term ingress throttling for noisy keys to protect checkout flows.

Impact so far: error rate fell from ~5.4% to ~1.8% over the last 20 minutes, throughput is recovering to ~92% of expected, p95 latency trending down toward baseline. We will keep the banner on your side up until we confirm stability for 60m.

Next communications:
- 16:25 PDT: planned next customer update (I will own);
- 17:00 PDT: bridge to confirm long-term remediation and runbook.

We will follow up with a post-incident write-up including root cause, timeline, and long-term fixes (cache policy changes + autoscale tuning). Attached are the error snapshot and a draft comm for your review.

Appreciate the quick heads-up and patience — we know this impacts peak revenue flows.

— Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 11:30:00 Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <e.chen@hudsonretail.com>, David Park <david.park@hudsonretail.com>, Hudson SRE <sre@hudsonretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Final update: stability confirmed (post-stabilization readout)

David/Emily —
Final readout: after three hours of monitoring and stepped remediation we confirmed service stability across the affected checkout routes. Key outcomes: 
- No customer-visible data loss or content corruption detected; the fallback quantized model returned functionally equivalent outputs for checkout flows (we validated via prompt-set sampling).
- Billing window for potential SLA credits: 2027-04-09T15:00:00-07:00 through 2027-04-09T16:00:00-07:00.
- Root cause summary: unexpected token-length skew from a marketing-driven metadata payload increase causing KV-cache thrash + autoscale delay under bin-packed allocation.
- Remediations enacted: cache policy changes (shorter TTLs for large-request keys), autoscale tuning to avoid delayed reaction on traffic surges, and an opt-in per-account routing guard to detect token-length distribution anomalies and proactively roll traffic to compatible model variants.

Next steps:
- We will deliver a post-incident report (timeline, artifact links, suggested SLA credit) by end of Monday 2027-04-12.
- We recommend a short joint run (30m) next week to validate the guardrails against Hudson's upcoming marketing campaign.

If you want a short exec digest for your board, Grace has prepared a one-page summary (attached).

— Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: post-incident-draft.pdf, exec-digest-onepager.docx
